item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could activate Jazz Chisholm Jr. as soon as Tuesday, raising questions about Anthony Volpe's role.
Nothing is set yet, manager Aaron Boone said Sunday, according to New York Daily News reporter Gary Phillips. The update came before the Yankees played the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix.
Chisholm sprained his right thumb Sept. 8. The Yankees recalled Volpe, 25, from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Sept. 10. They had optioned him in early August after promoting shortstop George Lombard Jr.
Volpe has played second base since then and has produced remarkable numbers.
Through Saturday, he has gone 9-for-31 in nine games since his recall. That is a .290 average with a .333 on-base percentage, a .452 slugging percentage and a .785 OPS.
He has one home run, two doubles, seven RBIs and four runs scored. Volpe has walked twice, struck out four times and stolen four bases without being caught.
Anthony Volpe's Future Is Still Not Known
Volpe could also see time at third base in the coming days. Boone fielded a question about using Volpe there, Phillips reported.
"We'll see," Boone said. "First things first, getting Jazz back and then we'll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it."
Volpe also addressed the idea, Phillips reported.
He said the Yankees have not talked to him about playing third base before the regular season ends. He said he felt comfortable there the few times he played third base in the minors.
At Triple-A, Volpe made 19 starts at second base, 15 at shortstop and three at third base.
Chisholm is batting .232 with 19 home runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games this season.
The Yankees open their final homestand Tuesday with a doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays. They entered Sunday at 89-65.
Trent Grisham is Out for the Regular Season
Boone said the Yankees do not expect to activate Trent Grisham before the regular season ends, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported.
Grisham could still be on the playoff roster, Boone said.
The New York Post's Greg Joyce reported that roster complications are part of the reason. The Yankees would have to send a player down and could not recall him for 10 days, Joyce reported.
Joyce contrasted that with activating Grisham directly onto the playoff roster.
Grisham has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 5 with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. He left a Sept. 4 game against the San Diego Padres in the third inning. It is his second right hamstring strain of the season.
Grisham is batting .211 with 18 home runs and 59 RBIs this season. The 29-year-old will be a free agent after the season.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees Face Anthony Volpe Decision After Jazz Chisholm Jr. News appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we'll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who's finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he'll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn't totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He's always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn't have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We've seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who'll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night's hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.
How to watch
Location: Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ
First pitch: 4:10 pm ET
TV broadcast: YES, DBACKS.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), ESPN 620 AM, La Campesina 101.9 FM & 860 AM (AZ)
Online stream: MLB.tv (out-of-market only), Gotham Sports App
For updates, follow us on BlueSky, Twitter, and Instagram, and like us on Facebook.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] The only Yankees position without multiple Silver Slugger winners should send message to front office
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: The New York Yankees aren't nicknamed the Bronx Bombers for no reason. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees aren't nicknamed the Bronx Bombers for no reason. For that reason, they've been well represented in the Louisville Slugger Silver Slugger Awards throughout the years. The Yankees have multiple representatives at every position except for one: shortstop.
This is in part because the award was first introduced in 1980, meaning that franchise greats and champions like Phil Rizzuto and Frank Crosetti missed the boat by a large margin. Another mitigating factor is that New York had one player dominate the position for much of the Silver Slugger era. That, of course, is Derek Jeter, who had a stranglehold on the position for the better part of two decades, taking home the award five times himself.
But while it seems like yesterday, Jeter's last big league season was in 2014. Since then, the position has looked pretty bleak. From 2015 through the present day, the Yankees have gotten a .715 OPS out of the position, which ranks 15th in the majors during that span.
That number includes the Didi Gregorius years, which included some very fine performances. Gregorius hit 97 homers in pinstripes over five seasons, while slashing .269/.313/.446. That's nothing to sneeze at, but he was never the AL's best hitter at the position during his time here.
Gregorius left following the 2019 season, and since then, things have been bleak. From 2020 onward, we have mostly been dealing with Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Anthony Volpe at short. In that time period, Yankees shortstops have produced a .668 OPS, ranking 26th in baseball.
The Yankees can't continue getting subpar offensive production out of the shortstop position
Right now, the hope for the future is George Lombard Jr. The club's top prospect got off to a hot start, but since then, he's cooled substantially. It's too early to write him off just yet, especially at just 21 years old. However, the Yankees can't afford to get into another Volpe-esque holding pattern where years go by and no material improvements are made.
That leaves the front office with an interesting conundrum. Shortstops who can hit and field don't grow on trees, and while Brian Cashman passed on a generational shortstop free-agent class to sign IKF to keep the seat warm for Volpe, he cannot afford to repeat the same lethargic approach to the position.
Ideally, Lombard Jr. snatches the job for the next 20 years with a strong finish to 2026, a postseason to remember, and a spring training that eliminates all doubt. Jeter met with the promising youngster to advise him on the responsibilities that lie ahead. Now we'll see if he took those lessons to heart.
But if we come to the conclusion of New York's 2026 campaign and haven't seen Lombard Jr. show signs that he can consistently rise to the occasion; the Yankees must be opportunistic when it comes to pursuing upgrades.
After being wrapped up in rumors at the trade deadline, it's thought that the Angels could revisit trade talks for Zach Neto in the offseason. Another possible scenario is that the Astros follow the Kyle Tucker path and trade Jeremy Peña this winter ahead of his final year of team control.
In an ideal situation, the Yankees could acquire a player like Neto or Peña while retaining Lombard Jr. to hedge their bets. Worst-case scenario: Lombard Jr. busts, and the team has a high-end veteran to man the position. Best-case scenario: they have to undertake some shuffling, but Lombard Jr. is a star, and the team is deeper and better for it.
What can't happen is the Yankees put all their eggs in the Lombard Jr. bucket, and then miss out on young stars in their prime and let the position languish for another half-decade. The time to wait and see is over, and the time to be bold is now.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] La Novia De Anthony Volpe Vuelve A Ser Noticia En Arizona Mientras La Estrella De Los Yankees Se Enfrenta A Los Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Inna Zeyger
item.description: PHOENIX — Anthony Volpe tiene muchas cosas en las que centrarse ahora que los Yankees se preparan para octubre. Su novia, Elle Jowett, por su parte, ha encontrado un rincón mucho más tranquilo de Arizona. Jowett volvió a ser tema de conversación fuera del campo entre los Yankees el domingo, después de compartir unas fotos de una excursión por el sendero Cathedral Rock Trail, en Sedona, mientras Volpe y el equipo de Nueva York estaban en el estado para disputar su serie de tres partidos contra lo
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Anthony Volpe tiene muchas cosas en las que centrarse ahora que los Yankees se preparan para octubre. Su novia, Elle Jowett, por su parte, ha encontrado un rincón mucho más tranquilo de Arizona.
Jowett volvió a ser tema de conversación fuera del campo entre los Yankees el domingo, después de compartir unas fotos de una excursión por el sendero Cathedral Rock Trail, en Sedona, mientras Volpe y el equipo de Nueva York estaban en el estado para disputar su serie de tres partidos contra los Diamondbacks de Arizona.
La modelo, afincada en Nueva York, se fue de excursión a Cathedral Rock y compartió unas fotos en las que aparece meditando en el sendero. Jowett llevaba una camiseta deportiva y unos leggings mientras posaba con el característico paisaje de rocas rojas y el entorno desértico de Sedona de fondo.
El momento hace que una publicación sobre un estilo de vida que, por lo demás, sería muy sencilla, adquiera un toque relacionado con los Yankees.
Mientras Jowett disfrutaba del paisaje de Arizona, Volpe seguía inmerso en una aventura de septiembre muy diferente, a unos 190 kilómetros de distancia, en Phoenix.
Jowett sale a la luz durante una racha importante de los Yankees
Los Yankees ya se han asegurado su participación en el béisbol de octubre, tras conseguir su tercera clasificación consecutiva para la postemporada. Lo que aún está por decidir es su recorrido en la postemporada.
El sábado nos volvió a recordar que los partidos que quedan no son para tomárselos a la ligera.
Arizona venció a Nueva York por 5-3 gracias a un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada que dio la victoria a su equipo. Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 89-65, lo que les mantiene bajo presión en la recta final de la temporada regular.
Volpe participó de lleno en el ataque de Nueva York.
Jugó como segunda base, conectó 1 de 4, bateó un sencillo en la quinta entrada y luego anotó la primera carrera de los Yankees gracias a un fly de sacrificio de Ben Rice.
Esto convierte a la serie en otra buena prueba de fuego de octubre para un equipo de los Yankees que ya tiene asegurada su participación más allá de la temporada regular.
El papel de Volpe en los Yankees ha cambiado radicalmente
El puesto de Volpe en la alineación se ha convertido en uno de los temas más interesantes que rodean al equipo.
Los Yankees lo bajaron a la Triple A durante la segunda mitad de la temporada tras sus problemas ofensivos. Durante su etapa en las ligas menores, Volpe empezó a jugar de segunda base, alejándose de la posición de campocorto que definió sus primeros años en las Grandes Ligas.
Más tarde, Nueva York lo volvió a llamar después de que la lesión en el pulgar de Jazz Chisholm Jr. dejara un hueco en el cuadro.
Volpe anunció su regreso a lo grande el 10 de septiembre, con una actuación de tres hits y cinco carreras impulsadas, que incluyó un grand slam en la victoria de los Yankees por 10-3 sobre Colorado. Después admitió que nada de lo relacionado con su regreso estaba garantizado cuando Nueva York lo envió inicialmente a la Triple A.
Volpe está aprovechando al máximo su segunda oportunidad con los Yankees
Y lo que es más importante para los Yankees, Volpe no ha dejado que ese memorable partido de regreso sea un caso aislado.
En sus últimos ocho partidos hasta el domingo, este jugador de 25 años tenía un promedio de bateo de .296, con un porcentaje de embasado de .345 y un porcentaje de slugging de .481, lo que le da un OPS de .826. Consiguió ocho hits en 27 turnos al bate durante ese periodo, incluyendo dos dobles y un jonrón, además de impulsar siete carreras.
Esas cifras suponen una respuesta significativa por parte de un jugador cuyo futuro en los Yankees parecía mucho menos seguro cuando el club lo envió de vuelta a la Triple A.
El regreso de Volpe también vino acompañado de un cambio de posición. En lugar de recuperar inmediatamente el puesto de campocorto, ha estado jugando en segunda base mientras los Yankees evalúan cómo podría encajar su cuadro interior en octubre.
Este experimento ha añadido otra dimensión a su resurgimiento de final de temporada.
No consiguió ningún hit en sus cuatro turnos al bate durante la victoria del viernes por 9-2 contra Arizona, pero el sábado respondió con un sencillo y una carrera anotada.
La tendencia general sigue siendo alentadora.
Volpe llegó a esta recta final con la necesidad de demostrar que su paso por la Triple A había dado frutos tangibles. En lugar de volver simplemente porque una lesión le había dejado un hueco, ha empezado a dar a los Yankees motivos para seguir dándole oportunidades al bate.
Eso podría ser muy importante cuando el entrenador Aaron Boone empiece a decidir qué combinación de infield le da a Nueva York su mejor alineación para la postemporada.
Elle Jowett ha ido acaparando cada vez más la atención de los Yankees
La aparición de Jowett en Arizona no es la primera vez que su actividad en las redes sociales llama la atención en un momento importante de la temporada de Volpe.
Ella y Volpe se hicieron públicos como pareja durante la temporada de 2025 tras aparecer juntos en la gala Willow Grant de la Fundación Carlos Rodón en Greenwich, Connecticut.
Posteriormente, Jowett asistió a partidos de la postemporada de los Yankees, aunque la pareja ha mantenido en general su relación al margen de sus propias redes sociales.
A principios de este año, Jowett volvió a aparecer en los titulares tras compartir fotos de Los Ángeles más o menos cuando los Yankees enviaron a Volpe a la Triple A. Otros miembros de la gran familia de los Yankees interactuaron con esa publicación.
Más tarde, llamó la atención con otra publicación de modelaje coincidiendo con el regreso de Volpe a las Grandes Ligas.
Ahora, Arizona es el último punto de encuentro entre los mundos separados de la pareja.
El fin de semana de Jowett ha girado en torno a la meditación y al paisaje de rocas rojas de Sedona. El de Volpe, por su parte, ha estado marcado por un equipo de los Yankees , que se dirige a la postemporada, que ha tenido que lidiar con una derrota en la última entrada, un panorama cambiante en el cuadro y decisiones cada vez más importantes sobre su alineación para octubre.
Los contextos no podrían ser más diferentes.
Pero ahora que octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina, ambas han vuelto a poner la vida fuera del campo de Volpe al mismo nivel que uno de los tramos más decisivos de su temporada con los Yankees.
¿Qué le parece? Deje su comentario a continuación.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] What the Yankees' Lineup Should Look Like Without Aaron Judge In October
item.dc:creator: Michael Zeno; Unknown
item.description: Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be. A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be. A scenario is now potentially unfo
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be.
A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be.
A scenario is now potentially unfolding that would have only appeared in Boone's nightmares: a postseason without the best hitter in baseball, with a lineup that struggled mightily without him. Even if they seemed to gradually improve as time went on, particularly in August, it would be a massive blow if he cannot return.
You can't replace a guy like Judge midseason; you can merely do your best to make up for his absence. Fortunately, on a platoon-heavy team like this, they should have plenty of options to build a lineup without him for the playoffs.
What the playoff lineup should look like against right-handed pitching
- Ben Rice (DH)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Luis García Jr. (1B)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Austin Wells (C)
- Ryan McMahon (3B)
This lineup simultaneously features the easiest decisions, but also the roughest circumstances. Having a guy like Judge as the ultimate lineup balancer who mashed both lefties and righties allowed you to use plenty of left-handed hitters at the top of the order, something that the team has in abundance.
The best right-handed hitter on the roster without Judge is hard to pinpoint, especially since all of them are significantly worse against same-handed pitching. Heliot Ramos might just be the best option to bat highest among them, which would be cleanup in this scenario.
It's not an ideal situation in the slightest. Even if you don't think it makes sense to bat Ramos that high because of his struggles against righties, there is some merit to breaking up the team's many left-handed bats. In a lineup that will likely only feature one other righty, it has to be considered.
The fate of this lineup when they're out there, which would likely be mostly after a potential Wild Card Series with the Red Sox, would hinge on the middle. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. got hot in August and helped the offensive turnaround begin, but both are heavily streaky bats with contact issues. If they go cold, this lineup might limp through games like they did in July.
What the playoff lineup should look like against left-handed pitching
- Paul Goldschmidt (1B)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Ben Rice (DH)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- Anthony Volpe/José Caballero (3B)
- Austin Wells (C)
Here's where it gets interesting. How far do you lean into the platoons on a team with several players designated to specifically hit lefties, especially against a team that will likely lean heavily on those types of pitchers in Boston?
Many Yankees fans believe that it would be improper to take a guy like García, who is likely the team's second-best pound-for-pound hitter with Judge injured, out of the lineup, but you don't really have a choice here. He's slashing just .238/.274/.363 against lefties, while Goldschmidt has been among the team's best hitters against them for the last two seasons. Add in Rice's improvements against same-handed pitching, and it just needs to be done.
Using him in a different position is also just not happening. He has not played second base, where he was extremely poor, since 2025. The only position he's played this season is first base. If he wasn't so dreadful out there, maybe he could replace Chisholm, a mediocre hitter against lefties in his own right.
Speaking of defense, you might notice the lack of Amed Rosario, and that's intentional. Rosario's use on this roster was almost exclusively predicated on his ability to hit left-handed pitching, but he's been significantly worse at it this season. Add in his truly dreadful defense, and you have a conundrum.
Anthony Volpe is a better hitter than José Caballero, but there are questions about how his arm strength would play at third, where he's also very inexperienced with just three games played in Triple-A. Caballero would probably get the nod here, but he's someone who just plays better off the bench with his speed and versatility.
It's also an aggressive placement for Lombard, batting fifth in his first career playoff game. The results haven't quite been there yet for him, but he's always been significantly better against lefties and should be slid up the lineup and be treated as one of those platoon bats who are there to hit that handedness, even if it might lead to consequences in the bullpen.
Boston is loaded with left-handed pitching from the rotation to the bullpen, so there will be few opportunities to get to a guy like García on the bench. The rest of the bench would be situational with pinch runners and pinch hitters.
Things ultimately look particularly shallow, but is there a chance that some last-minute reinforcements could help out?
Could Trent Grisham or Giancarlo Stanton return to provide relief?
It seems unlikely, especially early in the postseason, but the Yankees are refusing to shut the door on either Trent Grisham's or Giancarlo Stanton's return.
Grisham, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain earlier this month, was revealed to be "pretty far along" in his running program, and Boone said it's not out of the question that he returns in the season's final days, although an exact timeline for that has not been spelled out. If Grisham is physically ready to get back on the field, it would provide a boost, even if he might not be starting over Jones at this point.
Stanton, who's been out since April due to two separate calf strains and a re-aggravation, has continued to hit through his rehab, but hasn't resumed running as of last Sunday. Considering how it took several weeks for him to even get close to back from injury with his running program last time, this likely doesn't put him in play until the ALCS at the earliest.
While Stanton seems significantly less likely to get into a game again this season, there is a path for Grisham. The team could use him and Ramos in a platoon situation to add yet another lefty to the lineup against right-handed pitching. They could also utilize him as a pinch hitter on a larger bench than usual, due to the team's propensity to carry fewer than 13 pitchers in the Wild Card Series.
The real question for Grisham is defensive. While Jones has absolutely looked shaky in center field, the struggles of Grisham out there are well documented. Add in his diminished athleticism and likely balky hamstring straight off an injury, would it be better if the team just chanced it by throwing him in right field when he plays?
He hasn't played the position since a disastrous error lost the Brewers the 2019 Wild Card Game against the Nationals, but playing it at Yankee Stadium is significantly easier than dealing with the spacious center field. Of course, this is something the Yankees would have to determine their willingness to do beforehand and have him practice the position, so what plans they have will be determined by that.
As for Stanton if he's ever medically able to get back? There just might not be any room for him with Rice as the permanent DH. You don't want to take the bat out of either of their hands, and with the team seemingly having to juggle multiple guys coming off soft-tissue injuries, can they afford to use a roster spot for a designated pinch hitter as they did with 2022 Matt Carpenter?

item.title: [heavy.com] Cardinals Receive Strong Message Involving Yankees' Anthony Volpe
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Razo
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals missed the playoffs this season and will need to head back to the drawing board to build a team that can qualify for the postseason next year. Moreover, the question is what moves they should make to improve the team to challenge the Chicago Cubs and Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central. It’s been a wild 2026 MLB season for Anthony Volpe, who was optioned to Triple-A in August and then recalled in September. Still, it might be in the 25-year-old’s best interest to get a fr
item.content:encoded:
The St. Louis Cardinals missed the playoffs this season and will need to head back to the drawing board to build a team that can qualify for the postseason next year.
Moreover, the question is what moves they should make to improve the team to challenge the Chicago Cubs and Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central.
It’s been a wild 2026 MLB season for Anthony Volpe, who was optioned to Triple-A in August and then recalled in September. Still, it might be in the 25-year-old’s best interest to get a fresh start elsewhere.
Since reaching the majors in 2023, Volpe has been hitting .225 with 432 hits, 54 homers, 218 RBIs, and 241 runs scored in 537 games for the New York Yankees in his career, per StatMuse.
Despite this production during his four seasons in Pinstripes, FanSided’s Robert Murray believes that the Cardinals could be the change of scenery that Volpe needs after a rollercoaster career with the Yankees.
“Anthony Volpe would be a really good, buy-low option for the Cardinals,” Murray wrote in a Sept. 19 article. “Volpe was supposed to be the Yankees’ long-term answer at shortstop. Instead, he struggled mightily and fluctuated between the majors and minors.
“The Yankees still believe in Volpe and want to hold him, so a trade might be considered unlikely. But this is something that other teams will sniff around this offseason, I believe, and Bloom – who has previously worked with the Red Sox and Rays – should have plenty of familiarity in dealing with the Yankees.”
Anthony Volpe Could Boost Trade Value In the Coming Weeks
Since being recalled on Sept. 9, Volpe has performed well. Entering Sept. 20, Volpe has been batting .290 with nine hits, a home run, seven RBIs, and four runs scored in seven games, per StatMuse.
Moreover, if Volpe can end the season on a high note and have a productive postseason, his trade value might increase, and a team like the Cardinals could feel they can tap into his potential.
Volpe will have an opportunity to step up like every Yankee in that lineup, given that Aaron Judge is back on the injured list. New York can’t replace Judge with one batter, but they can do so with everyone chipping in.
Cardinals, Yankees Get Compelling Trade Idea
Recently, Christopher Kline of FanSided floated a trade idea that would send Volpe along with LHP Brent Headrick and LHP Kyle Carr to the Cardinals for 24-year-old shortstop Masyn Winn.
“The Yankees’ lack of fundamental soundness on the defensive end has bitten them in the you-know-what all season, just like it did last year,” Kline wrote in a Sept. 16 article. “The hope was that top prospect George Lombard Jr. could steady the ship at shortstop, but he has stacked up errors left and right.
“It’s too early to write off the 21-year-old long term, but he could serve more comfortably at third or second — which is notable, since Jazz Chisholm Jr. is about to [be a free agent]. Winn immediately alleviates a ton of defensive issues for the Yankees, while his weaker bat would be well-protected in the American League’s most potent lineup.”

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees suffered a tough loss on Saturday night, falling to the Arizona Diamondbacks 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s two-run walk-off home run in the ninth inning.
The loss came after the Yankees twice held a lead earlier in the game. New York broke through in the fifth inning when Austin Wells, Anthony Volpe and José Caballero opened the frame with consecutive singles to load the bases. Ben Rice followed with a sacrifice fly that brought home Wells and put the Yankees ahead 1-0.
Arizona answered in the bottom half of the inning, taking a 2-1 lead on Jordan Lawler’s two-run triple. Both runs were unearned against Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, who committed a fielding error on a sacrifice bunt during the inning.
New York responded quickly in the sixth. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a solo home run before Wells put the Yankees back in front with his 13th home run of the season. Both home runs came against Arizona reliever Kevin Ginkel.
Schlittler ran into trouble again in the bottom of the sixth after issuing two walks and allowing a single to load the bases with nobody out. Corbin Carroll tied the game with a sacrifice fly, but Schlittler struck out the next two batters to escape further damage.
Schlittler completed six innings, allowing three runs on three hits with three walks and six strikeouts over 98 pitches. Only one of the three runs was earned, and his season earned-run average dropped to 1.94.
Neither team scored again until the ninth, when Smith ended the game with his two-run homer off Michael Fulmer.
The Yankees will finish the series Sunday at 4:10 p.m. Will Warren will face Corbin Burnes.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees lose to Diamondbacks in walk-off fashion
item.dc:creator: Joshua Diemert

item.content:encoded:
One would figure that with Cam Schlittler going on Saturday night, this would be the game for the Yankees to win if they had any hope for a last-ditch AL East comeback, but something about Arizona wore down the likely Cy Young Award winner tonight. The Snakes were pesky, annoying, and other terms my editors won’t let me use while in the batter’s box tonight, finally breaking through on a Pavin Smith walk-off home run, to win it, 5-3.
Right off the top, I need to be grumpy about something. Nobody likes West Coast games and nobody likes the fact that every time the Yankees are on the West Coast, they play more night games than day games. This goes double for West Coast Yankee fans, because the beautiful thing about cheering for an East Coast team is they start playing when you get off work, or when you’re just finishing your Saturday morning coffee, the game takes three hours and you have the evening to yourself. That doesn’t happen on these trips.
Now, the Diamondbacks were celebrating the only World Series title in history, 25 years ago this season. I get it, you want to have a special event, the team isn’t very good so the end of the season starts to drag a little bit, you want a little spice. I even respect the cheek of waiting until the Yankees are in town. What I don’t respect is being completely incapable of running a functioning ceremony. The Yankees have Old Timer’s Day every year, they designate a special start time and at that time, the festivities have concluded and we can get down to the reason we’re all here, to watch a baseball game, which I don’t think is an unreasonable expectation at a baseball stadium with a baseball team in town.
The Diamondbacks started their pregame ceremonies at 4:30pm local time, with a scheduled 5:10pm first pitch. They absolutely blew past that in a way that, in my opinion, was both unprofessional and downright insulting. The four clocks I have ready access to in my apartment agreed: Brandon Pfaadt didn’t throw his first offering to Ben Rice until 5:42pm. This was an absolute joke of a start to the series’ second game. That all this happened in a city I’m predisposed to dislike already was…whatever the anti-cherry on top. I also firmly don’t like the existence of Phoenix as a city in general so I was always going to be ticked off watching this one.
I said in the gamethread that we had maybe begun to develop outsized expectations for Cam Schlittler. He’s been SO good, for long enough, that we needed to remember the other team all drives nice cars and lives in nice houses too. While Cam did get through 4.1 innings without allowing a hit, the Diamondbacks pushed a pair of runs across in the fifth. Nolan Arenado reached with a one-out single, before Tim Tawa attempted to give himself up with a sac bunt. Schlittler couldn’t corral what should have been an out though, an error that put two men on, and #9 hitter Jordan Lawlar made him pay:
Funny enough, because Schlittler was charged with that error, both of the runs were unearned, and he still hasn’t allowed more than a single earned run in eight starts now. The Yankees would tie the game the next inning, but all those extra pitches taxed his right arm, and I think had a major impact on what would happen in the sixth.
Speaking of tying the game, Heliot Ramos was brought to New York because of his opposite field power. He stunk in his first taste of East Coast baseball, but has looked much more representative in his last 20 games, and flexed that oppo pop within moments of Schlittler getting back in the dugout:
Corbin Carroll ran down a sinking Anthony Volpe liner for the second out, a very nice play that loomed larger when Austin Wells stepped to the plate:
Wells is getting hot at the right time, with three home runs in his last five games and he’s actually been a league average hitter since August 1! The nice thing about being a good defensive catcher is if you can just not embarrass yourself at the plate, you’re a major asset for your team.
The good vibes only lasted until Cam got back on the mound though. I think the error and the triple shook him up a little, and we’ve seen this happen before. Schlittler’s a high-energy guy, when that energy is less than positive I do think he gets a little in his own head and starts to overthrow. He walked the first two batters of the inning on eight total pitches, completely uncompetitive at-bats that are just so out of whack with what he’s done so far this season.
A soft Geraldo Perdomo bunt loaded the bases, and Cam did seem to lock in at that point. Corbin Carroll did bring in the third Snakes run of the game — and the only earned for Cam — but the ace got both Arenado and Tawa to whiff to end the threat. It was a weird one for Schlittler tonight, but 6.0 IP and one earned run is what the line reads.
The bullpen wasn’t exactly dynamite in Cam’s stead; the Diamondbacks have the third-lowest strikeout rate in baseball and their ability to grind out at-bats showed, even if the Yankees got through eight innings keeping the game tied at three. This was a long, miserable game, and wasn’t helped by the fact the Yankees couldn’t really find the nine-run spark that they showed on Friday.
If nothing else, I got to re-hate Michael Fulmer, and all those feelings from 2016 sprung forth anew. He walked the leadoff batter to open the ninth, and gave up the walk-off dinger to Pavin Smith:
The division race is functionally over with the Rays’ win earlier today, as they restored their five-game lead. Get yourself set for the Wild Card, lock up home-field advantage for that series, and don’t get yourselves hurt. The Yankes finish this series tomorrow with Will Warren on the hill. First pitch is supposedly at 4:10pm Eastern, but we’ll see.

item.dc:creator: Jake Rogers
item.description: The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it. New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a three-game series against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix.
New York won the first game of the series 9-2 on Friday. Game 2 is slated to begin at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday.
Before Saturday’s game, the Yankees announced a surprising lineup decision involving José Caballero.
New York Yankees Announce Interesting José Caballero Decision
Surprisingly, José Caballero will start in center field for the Yankees on Saturday. Caballero has played 11 innings in center this season and recorded 15 innings at the position last year.
Meanwhile, Spencer Jones, the Yankees’ primary center fielder, is out of the lineup with a sore left foot.
The New York Post’s Greg Joyce wrote on X: Spencer Jones said he’s dealing with a sore left foot, which he chalked up to the wear-and-tear from playing on turf. But downplayed it, said he’s fine, just getting a day. “It’s no big deal,” Jones said.
Here is the Yankees’ full lineup for Saturday:
- Ben Rice DH
- Cody Bellinger LF
- Luis Garcia Jr. 1B
- Heliot Ramos RF
- George Lombard Jr. SS
- Austin Wells C
- Anthony Volpe 2B
- Ryan McMahon 3B
- José Caballero CF
Starting Pitcher: RHP Cam Schlittler
Here is the Diamondbacks’ lineup:
- Laars Nootbar LF
- Ketel Marte 2B
- Gabriel Moreon C
- Geraldo Perdomo SS
- Corbin Carroll RF
- Nolan Arenado 3B
- Tim Tawa 1B
- Jesus Sanchez DH
- Jordan Lawlar CF
Starting Pitcher: Brandon Pfaadt
New York Yankees Right Now
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] How the Yankees Should Utilize Jazz Chisholm Jr. When He Returns
item.dc:creator: Joe Najarian; Unknown
item.description: With Aaron Judge likely done for the season, the New York Yankees will rely heavily on their other bats to pick up the slack. One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Chisholm, who was putting up an .832 OPS and .367 wOBA since August 4, is expected to be activated during the Yankees' final homestand this coming week. item.content:encoded:
With Aaron Judge likely done for the season, the New York Yankees will rely heavily on their other bats to pick up the slack.
One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Chisholm, who was putting up an .832 OPS and .367 wOBA since August 4, is expected to be activated during the Yankees' final homestand this coming week. Despite a very disappointing season as a whole, the 28-year-old's improved play is an extremely encouraging sign.
At the same time, Anthony Volpe has taken full advantage of his new opportunity at second base. When Chisholm went down, Volpe's improvements at the plate in Triple-A carried over to the major leagues and his production from the bottom of the order is a boon to the Yankees' offense. The 25-year old is slashing .296/.345/.481 in 29 plate appearances while also stealing four bases.
The problem is that the Yankees have three middle infielders looking for starting spots. George Lombard Jr. is firmly entrenched at shortstop, which necessitated Volpe's transition to second base. Of course, second base is Chisholm's natural position and the Yankees have gotten well-above average defense from him there.
This means one of these three will be the odd man out... or does it?
The Yankees should play Jazz Chisholm Jr. at third base again
When the Yankees acquired Chisholm at the trade deadline in 2024, they already had Gleyber Torres at second base. So they tested Chisholm out at third base to ensure both players would be in the starting lineup. Chisholm also saw time at the hot corner last year when DJ LeMahieu played second, until the Yankees eventually released the aging LeMahieu to move Chisholm back to his natural position.
Chisholm's defense suffered at third in 2025, as he was worth -3 Outs Above Average (per Baseball Savant). But his athleticism and dynamic skillset is far too great to leave him out of the lineup entirely, even if he's endured a down year. On the other hand, it would be foolish for the Yankees to sit Volpe while he's hot at the plate and adapting well to second.
While second base has two strong options, third base is a major weakness. Ryan McMahon has been atrocious since returning to the lineup on Sept. 1, hitting just .154/.214/.179 in 42 plate appearances; the abysmal offensive production far outweighs McMahon's steady defense, even if the Yankees are going to rely on run prevention in the postseason. Jose Caballero is also capable of playing third, but he's best suited as a bench player at this point.
Between Chisholm and Volpe, the former is better suited to play third due to his past experience. The latter has a grand total of three games and 22.0 innings at the hot corner, all of them in Triple-A.
This certainly isn't an ideal situation for Chisholm: he's struggled for much of the season, got injured when he started turning things around, and may need to play at a secondary position to accommodate a teammate.
But this would likely be the Yankees' best lineup without Aaron Judge, and if Chisholm wants to both win a World Series and secure a future in the Bronx, then moving over to third is the best thing he can do to help the team right now.
Joe Najarian is a writer for Yankees On SI, having previously covered the Yankees both for SI and additional sites since 2023. He also served as Deputy Editor for the Yankees, Mets and Orioles On SI sites, and additionally contributes to Athlon Sports and Men’s Journal covering Major League Baseball and other trending sports news. Joe is a graduate of Rutgers University in 2022, earning a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Media Studies.
Follow JoeNajarian

item.title: [CBS Sports] Three questions for Aaron Judge and the Yankees as injury casts doubt on slugger's playoff availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
item.description: Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). item.content:encoded:
Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). Captain Aaron Judge is less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him more than three months. Judge's status for the rest of the season is up in the air.
"I don't have a timeline on him. I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires," manager Aaron Boone said (via MLB.com). "... The reality is, we've had to play a lot of the season this year without him. There's no replacing a player who is as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations. Those don't change now."
The Yankees are always cagey about Judge's injuries. They declined to reveal the severity of the calf strain or give a timetable for his return. Generally speaking, Grade 1 calf strains (the least severe) require 2-3 weeks on the injured list, though calves are very tricky and easy to reinjury. They must be allowed to heal fully, otherwise you risk a more severe injury.
For all intents and purposes, the Yankees are locked into the top wild-card spot. They're six games up in the loss column on the Boston Red Sox, who currently sit in the second wild card spot, plus the Yankees won the season series and have the tiebreaker, so it's really a seven-game lead. New York can clinch the top wild-card spot as soon as Sunday.
The AL East title remains mathematically possible, but it is a long shot. The Yankees are four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the loss column with four head-to-head games remaining next week in the Bronx. The Rays only need to win one of those four games to clinch the season series and secure the tiebreaker, upping the difficulty for New York.
Just to lay it all out, here's what needs to happen for the Yankees to win the AL East, assuming they sweep those four games against the Rays and clinch the tiebreaker for themselves, which is a pretty big assumption:
- Rays go 6-3 or better: Rays win AL East
- Rays go 5-4: Yankees must go 9-0
- Rays go 4-5: Yankees must go 8-1
- Rays go 3-6: Yankees must go 7-2
- Rays go 2-7: Yankees must go 6-3
- Rays go 1-8: Yankees must go 5-4
- Rays go 0-9: Yankees must go 4-5
The Yankees have already clinched a postseason spot and winning the AL East was a long shot even with Judge. These last nine regular-season games are almost meaningless. If the AL East race gets interesting in a few days, the Yankees can shift gears, but the big picture takes priority this next week. Resting key relievers, lining up the rotation for the Wild Card Series, etc.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game," Cody Bellinger said (via MLB.com). "For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I'm fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody."
With the postseason less than two weeks away, Judge's calf injury creates a lot of questions for both him and the Yankees overall. Here are three questions for the man himself, and his team.
Three questions for Judge
1. Will he return for the postseason? This is really the only question, right? The Yankees are built around Judge being the best hitter in the world, and when he's not, the walls begin to cave in. New York had one of the lowest-scoring offenses in baseball when Judge was out with his rib injury. To paraphrase another New York baseball legend, Judge is the straw that stirs the drink.
Judge is eligible to come off the injured list next Sunday, the final day of the regular season. Roster-wise, he can return in time for the postseason. Health-wise, we have no idea. Calf strains are rarely 10-day absences, but that's what the Yankees have to hope is the case here. There's a very real chance the Yankees are without Judge for at least the Wild Card Series, and maybe longer.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason,” Aaron Judge said. “That’s definitely the plan.”
Said the calf strain involves the soleus muscle — which he said is more crucial to running and hitting — making it more difficult to play through.
2. Will he be himself at the plate? Judge did not go on a minor-league rehab assignment before returning from the rib injury and it showed. He went 4 for 23 (.174) with one walk and 13 strikeouts in his seven games back before the calf injury. His timing was not there at all. Judge's one homer came on a hanging breaking ball. Otherwise, pitchers threw fastballs by him consistently.
To put a number on it, Judge missed with 41% of his swings against fastballs in his seven games back, more than double the 19% league average. This is what it looks like when you miss with more than two out of every five swings against heaters:
It is not exactly a surprise a hitter who did not go on a rehab assignment after spending more than three months on the shelf looked out of sorts at the plate. Judge and the Yankees knew it would take him some time to get back up to speed at the plate, and they were willing to live with it. The goal was always to be ready for the postseason, not so much the regular season.
These last nine games aren't particularly important for the Yankees in the standings, but they were incredibly important to Judge. He needed at-bats to rediscover his timing at the plate, and get back to being the dominant hitter he's been throughout his career. The calf strain puts that on pause. Judge now has even fewer at-bats available to get back to being himself.
3. Will he be able to play the field? There is a scenario in which Judge plays through the calf strain as a full-time DH who doesn't run at 100% (or close to it). How the Yankees would align their defense in that scenario, I have no idea. Ben Rice is a full-time DH these days and also New York's best non-Judge hitter. Platoon-mates Luis Gárcia Jr. and Paul Goldschmidt are first basemen.
Unless the Yankees do something unexpected, like put Gárcia back at second base (where he was terrible defensively) or Rice back behind the plate (where he was also terrible defensively), slotting Judge in at DH means one of the team's most productive hitters will have to sit. This is something the Yankees will worry about when the time comes, and not a second sooner.
Three questions for the Yankees
1. Where will the righty pop come from? The Yankees have a very lefty-heavy lineup and Judge's righty heft provides important balance. Only the Cleveland Guardians have gotten fewer plate appearances from righties this season. Friday's lineup against Arizona Diamondbacks lefty Eduardo Rodriguez could be what the Yankees run out there against lefties in October:
- 1B Paul Goldschmidt, RHB
- LF Cody Bellinger, LHB
- RF Heliot Ramos, RHB
- DH Ben Rice, LHB
- 3B Amed Rosario, RHB
- CF Spencer Jones, LHB
- SS George Lombard Jr., RHB
- C Austin Wells, LHB
- 2B Anthony Volpe, RHB
Goldschmidt and Ramos are lefty mashers. Bellinger and Rice are very productive left-on-left hitters. Jones has performed well against lefties as a big leaguer, though his minor-league track record against southpaws isn't great. Rosario is having his worst season against lefties. The 7-8-9 spots are unlikely to make an impact offensively, regardless of the pitcher's handedness.
That lineup would look much more imposing with Judge in the No. 3 spot. Perhaps this is not such a big concern though? Since trade deadline day, the Yankees have the highest batting average (.289) and on-base percentage (.362) against lefties, and the third-highest slugging percentage (.456) despite Judge not playing much, and not being much of a factor when he did play.
In all likelihood the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, and Boston has three quality lefty starters (Jake Bennett, Ranger Suárez, Payton Tolle) and a shutdown lefty relief tandem (Aroldis Chapman, Erik Miller). To beat the Red Sox, the Yankees will need their righty hitters to produce, and now the status of their best right-handed hitter is in question.
2. Will the pitching hold up? Despite not having Judge for more than three months, the Yankees have the American League's best run differential (+143) and second-best record (89-64). They can thank their pitching staff. New York has allowed only 3.68 runs per game this year, the fewest in baseball. Since trade deadline day, it's an incredible 3.37 runs allowed per game.
There are some cracks beginning to form, however. Gerrit Cole has surrendered eight home runs in his last three starts, including five on a four-seam fastball that is no longer the dominant pitch it was at his peak. Max Fried's velocity has been down a tick since returning from a bone bruise in his elbow late last month. That injury has sent him to the injured list twice this year.
Cam Schlittler, the AL Cy Young favorite, has thrown a career-high 184 ⅔ innings with two regular-season starts remaining, plus the postseason. Key late-inning relievers Paul Blackburn, David Bednar, and Brent Headrick have worked a lot -- A LOT -- this season and have all shown a slight dip in velocity in recent weeks, which perhaps is a sign the workload is catching up to them.
Without Judge (and sometimes even with him), the Yankees are a run prevention team. Their superpower is a suffocating pitching staff that is among the best in baseball at limiting hard contact, particularly in the air. With Judge absent, the pitching staff and the ability to prevent runs in general will be of paramount importance. No Judge reduces the margin of error considerably.
3. What about their other injured players? Judge is not the only injured Yankee. Center field Trent Grisham has not played since Sept. 4 due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain. On Friday, Boone said Grisham is pretty far into his running program, and he could make it back before the end of the regular season. That would give the outfield a lift should Judge miss extended time.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. has not played since jamming his thumb sliding into second base on Sept. 8. Boone said Chisholm will come off the injured list when the Yankees return home next week. He's had a down year overall, but Chisholm was playing his best baseball of the season right before the injury. He's an important presence given his speed and defense in particular.
Left-hander Ryan Weathers is working his way back from a flexor strain. He last pitched Aug. 22. Weathers is throwing bullpen sessions, though Boone confirmed he won't return during the regular season. If/when Weathers does return, it will be as a reliever. He has bullpen experience and the Yankees could use middle relief help, but Weathers has to make it back first.
At minimum, Chisholm and Grisham would give the Yankees more options for their Judge-less lineup, even if they only platoon. It wouldn't be hard to find a role for Weathers, who had allowed no more than one run in six of his last seven starts before the injury. Bottom line though, the Yankees need Judge. Everything else is secondary to his return and effectiveness.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Jazz Chisholm Jr. Expected to Return for Yankees' Final Homestand Against Rays
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are getting closer to having Jazz Chisholm Jr. back in the lineup.
Manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm is expected to be activated from the 10-day injured list during New York's final regular-season homestand. The Yankees begin that homestand Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Chisholm has been sidelined since Sept. 10 after spraining his right thumb on a head-first slide into second base against the Colorado Rockies.
The second baseman has continued making progress during his recovery. Boone said Friday marked Chisholm's fourth straight day of hitting in the batting cages, while he has also resumed throwing on the field.
The Yankees have been using Anthony Volpe at second base while Chisholm recovers. His return will give Boone another option in the infield as New York manages its lineup during the final week of the regular season.
Chisholm was also swinging the bat well before the injury. He hit .375 with a .464 on-base percentage and .500 slugging percentage over his final seven games.
The 28-year-old has appeared in 134 games this season, batting .232 with 16 doubles, three triples, 19 home runs and 55 RBI in 461 at-bats.
Chisholm has also provided plenty of value on the bases. He has scored 68 runs and stolen 40 bases on 49 attempts while posting a .312 on-base percentage and .403 slugging percentage.
His return comes at an important point for New York. The Yankees entered Saturday with an 88-64 record and sat 4 games behind the Rays in the AL East.
New York is also dealing with the expected absence of Aaron Judge for the remainder of the regular season, making Chisholm's return another potential boost for the lineup.
For now, the Yankees will continue monitoring Chisholm's thumb as he works toward activation. If he remains on schedule, he should be back during the final homestand before the postseason begins.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Aaron Judge is on the injured list again, but the Yankees could get two key pieces back off of it by next week.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated on the upcoming homestand that begins Tuesday, Aaron Boone said Friday, after the second baseman landed on the IL last week with a right thumb sprain.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Friday marked his fourth day of hitting in a row after being shut down from baseball activities for about a week, while he has also been throwing the last couple of days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said before the Yankees’ 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
Trent Grisham, meanwhile, is “pretty far into his running progression” from a right hamstring strain and “doing well,” Boone said, putting him in position to be in play at the end of the regular season.
Before Judge’s calf strain, it was questionable whether there would be a lane for Grisham to get playing time if and when he returned.
But now it is possible he could return to center field at least against righties, bumping Spencer Jones to right field.
As for Ryan Weathers, the other Yankee trying to make it back in time for the playoffs (from a left forearm flexor strain), Boone acknowledged the lefty is “unlikely to get into a game before the end of the season.”
Weathers is set to throw a second bullpen session on Saturday, after which he could advance to facing hitters in live batting practice.
Whether that will give him enough time to show he should be part of the bullpen for the first round of the playoffs remains to be seen.
“We’ll see what our needs are and how he looks and if we feel like he’s ready to come in and be a contributor,” Boone said.
Anthony Volpe, who was back at second base, hit .348 with a .965 OPS and four steals in his first seven games since being called back up from Triple-A as an injury replacement for Chisholm.
He was 0-for-4 in Friday night’s win.

item.title: [Yardbarker] New York Yankees Make Spencer Jones Announcement
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees open a series in Arizona on Friday night looking to rebound from a one-run loss and find more consistent production from a young outfielder who has shown both power and growing pains.
After falling 5-4 to the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday, the club posted its lineup for the first game against the Diamondbacks, and the most notable tweak involved Spencer Jones, via FantasyPros.
Jones had occupied the fifth spot in the order against Minnesota and finished without a hit while striking out five times. That performance prompted manager Aaron Boone to slide the 25-year-old down one place, into the sixth hole, for Friday’s contest.
The rest of the order features Paul Goldschmidt at first, Cody Bellinger in left, Heliot Ramos in right, Ben Rice as the designated hitter, Amed Rosario at third, George Lombard at short, Austin Wells behind the plate and Anthony Volpe at second. Jones will patrol center field.
The adjustment is modest on paper, yet it reflects the reality of a rookie season that has mixed encouraging numbers with stretches of swing-and-miss. Jones is hitting .252 with 59 hits, 10 home runs, 37 RBIs, 32 runs and nine stolen bases across 79 games.
Those totals represent real production for a player who made his major-league debut earlier this year after being selected in the first round of the 2022 draft out of Vanderbilt.
At 6-foot-7, 240 pounds, he possesses the kind of raw power that can change a game in a single swing, something he demonstrated with a three-run homer against the Twins just a few days earlier.
Still, five strikeouts in one night is the kind of night that forces a lineup shuffle. Boone has moved Jones around the order several times this season as the Yankees try to maximize his strengths while limiting damage against certain pitching looks.
The Diamondbacks series offers another chance to see whether a slightly lower spot in the batting order helps him settle in and put the ball in play more often.
New York arrives in Phoenix needing wins as the calendar moves deeper into September. A tight loss in Minnesota left little margin, and every at-bat from a developing bat like Jones carries extra weight.
The organization drafted him for his combination of size, athleticism and power; the challenge now is translating that package into more consistent contact at the highest level.
Friday’s lineup is a small tactical step in that process rather than a dramatic demotion.
Whether Jones responds with extra-base hits or continues to chase pitches remains to be seen. What is clear is that the Yankees still view him as part of their present and future outfield mix.
A drop from fifth to sixth is not a verdict on his season. It is simply the latest attempt to put a young player in a position where his next good swing can matter.

A fun weekend in prospect at Chase – at least, outside the lines, where the team will be celebrating the 25th anniversary of their World Series win against these same Yankees. The main party is taking place tomorrow night, but there are some things to note for tonight. Most relevantly to me who is recapping: Greg Schulte, the voice of the D-backs from their first Opening Day in 1998, through the end of the 2023 World Series, is making a return to the booth tonight. I've no idea how the sync between that and the TV broadcast will work out, but I think I am prepared to handle a little bit of lag for the evening.
With it being Friday night, and since I'm being robbed of most of my usual Friday night entertainment for recappage purposes – no eighties DJ on Twitch, no B-movie about killer hippopotami (they missed a trick by not calling the latter, Hippocalypse Now) – I will once again be tucking into my cider selection. Worked out well enough last Friday night, if my (slightly blurry) recollections are anything to go by. I think I have one untried flavor from the selection pack, plus a couple of "regular" brands in the fridge. You have been warned. Tim should be back for the final series next weekend, both you and my liver will be pleased to hear. 🙂
Another narrative will be taking the first pitch of the game, with Paul Goldschmidt returning to Chase Field. I'm sure he'll still get a warm welcome, even though he is now 1,104 games (including the post-season) removed from the last time Goldy pulled on the Sedona Red. I was looked at the 2018 roster, and there aren't many people there who are still playing in the majors this season. Ketel Marte, obviously – he was the "baby" of the roster that year! – and Ildemaro Vargas, then still a rookie. A few starting pitchers, in Taijuan Walker, Robbie Ray and Patrick Corbin. That's about it, on a quick, non-structured glance. Let me know if I missed any!

The Yankees skipper said Chisholm is doing well and Friday was
item.content:encoded:
Yankees manager Aaron Boone delivered some injury updates ahead of Friday's series opener with the Diamondbacks in Arizona…
Jazz returning soon
Although the Yankees are losing Aaron Judge, likely, for the remainder of the regular season, they'll be activating Jazz Chisholm Jr. very soon.
Boone confirmed that the second baseman will return to the club during the team's final homestand, which starts Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees skipper said Chisholm is doing well and Friday was his fourth day in a row hitting. He's done a couple of days of throwing already and is "really close."
Chisholm was placed on the IL back on Sept. 10 with a sprained thumb after he jammed it sliding head-first into second base.
The Yankees infielder was on a tear before he was injured, slashing .375/.464/.500 with a home run over his last seven games. For the season, he's batting .232/.312/.403 with an OPS of .715 to go along with his 19 home runs, 40 stolen bases and 55 RBI.
The return of Chisholm would raise some questions regarding the team's roster. While Chisholm could take over for Max Schuemann, who is being called up to take Judge's spot, Anthony Volpe has been playing second base almost regularly in Chisholm's stead. How Boone juggles the playing time for both players will be worth monitoring.
Bad Weathers
On the other side of the return spectrum, LHP Ryan Weathers is "unlikely" to pitch before the end of the regular season, Boone revealed.
Weathers was placed on the IL in late August due to a left forearm flexor strain, and although the southpaw has made strides, there's not enough time on the regular season calendar to get him on the mound before the postseason starts. Boone did say that Weathers will have another side session on Saturday, and that could determine whether the team will use him in the playoffs.
"We'll see what our needs are and how he looks, and if we feel like he's ready to come in and be a contributor," Boone said.
In 25 starts this season, Weathers has pitched to a 3.60 ERA and a 1.22 WHIP. His last seven starts have been tremendous, though, pitching to a 2.27 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP.
Grisham rising
And finally, Trent Grisham is nearing a return as well.
Boone said the veteran outfielder is "pretty far" into his running progression and is doing well. He could be in play to be activated before the end of the season.
Grisham was placed on the IL on Sept. 5 with a right hamstring strain, the same injury he suffered back in June this season. If Grisham is able to return on the upcoming homestand, Boone will, again, have to juggle the roster as Spencer Jones and Heliot Ramos have played regularly in his absence. Though Judge's injury gives Grisham a runway to start, especially against right-handers.
In 121 games this season, Grisham is slashing .211/.308/.395 with an OPS of .703.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising move on Anthony Volpe.
Volpe has had success since being recalled, but George Lombard Jr. has taken over as the starting shortstop. So, Volpe's future in New York is very much up in the air.
New York will begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
New York Yankees Surprise Anthony Volpe Decision
Although Volpe has been playing better, he isn't guaranteed a spot on the Yankees playoff roster.
After New York clinched a playoff spot, Yankees analysts Bryan Hoch and Patrick Donnelly of MLB.com revealed the likely playoff roster, and they didn't have Volpe on it.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Aaron Judge, Heliot Ramos
DH: Ben Rice
SP: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole
RP: David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, Ryan Weathers, Will Warren
The Yankees leaving Volpe off the playoff roster would be a disappointing outcome for the shortstop. It also could signal the end of his tenure in New York as Lombard is the shortstop of the future.
Volpe is hitting .253 with 2 home runs and 26 RBIs this season with the Yankees.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot as New York will be hosting a Wild Card series again.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
However, despite clinching a playoff spot, the Yankees made it clear the job isn't finished. New York likely won't win the AL East again, which is frustrating, but the Yankees have confidence they can go on a deep playoff run.
The Yankees are 88-64 and 5 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the top spot in the AL East.

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Cómo responderán los jóvenes de Yankees en los playoffs?
item.dc:creator: Patrick Donnelly
item.description: Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre. item.content:encoded:
Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre.
Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida
Cody Bellinger, 76
Aaron Judge, 65
Paul Goldschmidt, 29
Trent Grisham, 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells, 21
Anthony Volpe, 21
Amed Rosario, 11
Ryan McMahon, 10
Ben Rice, 6
José Caballero, 3
Pero faltan algunos nombres en esa lista: El campocorto George Lombard Jr., el jardinero Spencer Jones, el primera base dominicano Luis García Jr. y el jardinero puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos. Ninguno de esos cuatro nunca ha jugado en la postemporada, ya sea con los Yankees o, como es el caso de García y Ramos, con sus equipos anteriores.
Ahora, es posible que algunos de los jugadores veteranos lesionados -- Grisham y Chisholm, específicamente -- puedan regresar a la alineación y enviar a algunos de esos nuevos rostros a la banca o fuera del roster de postemporada por completo. Pero es seguro decir que los Yankees van a contar con al menos algunos novatos en los playoffs el próximo mes, en su búsqueda de ganar su primera Serie Mundial desde el 2009.
Boone ha expresado que sus jóvenes y los recién llegados a los playoffs tienen otra ventaja sobre los jugadores en otros mercados.
"Jugar para los Yankees, jugar en Nueva York”, dijo, "tiene una manera de prepararte para la postemporada”.
Éste ha sido un año de transición en las Grandes Ligas. Consulta la primera ronda del Draft del 2023 si quieres pruebas. No menos de 19 de las 37 selecciones de primera ronda y de compensación han debutado en las Mayores, y muchos de ellos ya son jugadores clave en sus equipos.
"Los jugadores están llegando a las Grandes Ligas a un ritmo muy rápido ahora y a temprana edad”, manifestó el piloto de los Tigers, A.J. Hinch, quien ha dado la bienvenida a la tercera selección Max Clark y al favorito para Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, Kevin McGonigle, a Detroit este año. "No creo que se sientan tan impresionados por los grandes pasos que están dando”.
Para los Yankees, ese grupo incluye a Lombard, quien se ha aclimatado bien desde que fue subido a principios de agosto. Y Jones fue elogiado recientemente nada menos que por Aaron Judge, quien dijo que el jardinero novato "realmente ha evolucionado cada vez que ha sido subido, mejorando un poco más en cada ocasión”.
Por supuesto, habrá contratiempos en el camino. El miércoles, Jones se fue de 6-0 con cinco ponches y cometió un error cuando dejó caer un batazo en el jardín central. Y Lombard no pudo atrapar un roletazo del boricua Victor Caratini en la 13ª entrada que fue considerado un sencillo mientras los Mellizos vencían a los Yankees.
Pero cualquiera que siga el béisbol sabe que los días malos y las malas jugadas son parte del ciclo de crecimiento de un jugador de Grandes Ligas. La clave es aprender de ellos para poder limitarlos en el futuro. Y todo ello -- lo bueno, lo malo y lo ocasionalmente feo -- ayuda a preparar a un joven jugador para su primera vez jugando en el béisbol de octubre.
El mundo está a punto de descubrir lo preparados que están los Yankees jóvenes. Pero Jones ofreció un poco de tranquilidad el lunes mientras disfrutaba de la celebración en el vestuario después de la victoria en Target Field que aseguró otra clasificación de Nueva York para los playoffs.
"Creo que para nosotros, jugamos mejor cuando la multitud se vuelve más ruidosa", dijo. "Estoy bien emocionado por lo que está por venir”.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon before the playoffs.
New York clinched a playoff berth. They will likely be in the Wild Card series again, likely playing the Boston Red Sox for the second year in a row.
The Yankees are 88-64.
New York Yankees Could Bench Ryan McMahon
With the Yankees heading back to the playoffs, New York could have to make a difficult decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon.
McMahon is a solid glove-first third baseman, but he has struggled offensively since coming to New York. With that, Yankees analyst Pat Ragazzo of FanSided believes New York could remove McMahon from its playoff roster, or simply have him on the bench.
"Should Rosario's hot streak continue into the end of the regular season, the Yankees find a way to utilize him at third base during the postseason," Ragazzo wrote. "There's even a world where Jose Caballero slides to third, with Anthony Volpe available off the bench. McMahon will probably still get a roster spot, but they cannot play his bat regularly in the biggest games of the year. McMahon's bat creates a black hole in the Yankees' lineup, which they cannot afford to deploy in October.
"If not for his defense, McMahon would've likely been designated for assignment by now. And given his historically poor offensive numbers, it seems like it could be headed that way with McMahon under contract for another year at $16 million. The 31-year-old just has not worked out as a member of the Yankees. His time in pinstripes should come to an end sooner rather than later."
McMahon has one more year on his six-year, $70 million deal. Not having him on the playoff roster would be a tough look. Yet, his bat has struggled, and the Yankees could use Caballero at third, with Volpe as the primary backup infielder in the playoffs.
McMahon is hitting .210 with 10 home runs and 34 RBIs this season.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot and once again have World Series aspirations.
Although New York did clinch a playoff spot, the Yankees know the job is not done.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
The Yankees are set to begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
